solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Locums, accepting pressure, give a lot back

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the reversed letters take the pressure letter inside them
back means the joined words give and a lot are read in reverse order

parts.note: to give is to sag, as a rope gives under weight
pots, as in pots of money, means a lot
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Temporary doctors take on a heavy workload and hand a great deal back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locums' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition; 'give' is the verb to sag, not to hand over.
explanation.definitionFit: Locums are temporary stand-in doctors, so they are stopgaps filling a vacancy for a short while.

clue.text: Ulster ground hosting grand golf contest

indicators.note: hosting means having guests inside, so the rearranged letters hold the two G letters
ground as in ground down, so the letters of Ulster are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish course hosts a major golf tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a golf course but is the past tense of grind: ULSTER rearranged to STRULE takes in GG.
explanation.definitionFit: A struggle is a fight or hard-fought tussle between opponents.

clue.text: Start running group

parts.note: a machine that is on is running
a set is a group

explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning, as in the onset of winter.

clue.text: Goes OTT, as sit-down protester often does?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: becomes overexcited, goes over the top
second meaning, literally: a protester sitting in the road is lifted and taken off by police

explanation.walkthrough: OTT is short for over the top. The second reading is literal: police remove a seated demonstrator bodily.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes losing self-control through enthusiasm, and literally describes being lifted and removed.

clue.text: Porcine mammal upended mushroom with a piercing yell

indicators.note: upended means turned upside down, so in a down clue the mushroom is read bottom to top

parts.note: a cep is a porcini mushroom

indicators.note: piercing means going into, so A goes inside the yell

parts.note: a cry is a yell

explanation.surface: A pig-like animal flips a mushroom over with a shrill scream.
explanation.definitionFit: The peccary is a pig-like hoofed mammal of the Americas, related to swine.

clue.text: In the future, share whatever part remains

parts.note: something a week off is still in the future
a cut is a share of the takings

explanation.surface: Someone promises that later on they will split whatever is left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the future' is not a time indicator here: as in 'the holidays are a month off', OFF means still to come.
explanation.definitionFit: An offcut is the leftover scrap after cutting material to size, the piece that remains.

clue.text: In poverty since employee (male) exposed husband

parts.note: from can mean since, as in from Monday
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
a tom is a male cat
out means revealed or exposed

explanation.surface: A worker has been poor ever since a man revealed her husband's secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Living hand to mouth means having just enough to eat, with nothing saved: being poor.

clue.text: Named driver's caution delivered verbally, being required

parts.note: to be called is to be named

indicators.note: delivered verbally means spoken aloud, so we enter the word that sounds like the golfer's warning

parts.note: a golfer hitting a drive shouts fore as a warning

explanation.surface: A named motorist's warning was given in speech, as the situation demanded.
explanation.walkthrough: The driver is a golfer using a driver club, not a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Called for means needed or demanded, as in a situation that called for tact.

clue.text: Striking red songbird in another's nest to start with

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: to start with means taking the first letter of each of the following words

parts.note: first letter of in
first letter of another's
first letter of nest

explanation.surface: A songbird lays its egg in another bird's nest, like a cuckoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian is a bright reddish-auburn hair colour, named after the Venetian painter's favoured shade.

clue.text: For contracting, chooses the right book

indicators.note: contracting means holding within, so the answer sits inside the words chooses the right

explanation.surface: For a contract, someone picks the correct book.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament telling of the Jewish queen of Persia.

clue.text: Again tried to pass weapon back

indicators.note: back means the weapon's name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a taser is a stun-gun weapon

explanation.surface: Someone attempts again to hand over a weapon, passing it back.
explanation.definitionFit: A student who resat an exam took it a second time, trying once more to get through.

clue.text: Sauce lost when cooking stew

indicators.note: cooking suggests ingredients being worked over, so the letters of sauce lost are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook lets the sauce go wrong while making a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassoulet is a French slow-cooked bean dish with meat, a kind of casserole.

clue.text: Leader of strategists in Carthage prepared to invade

indicators.note: prepared hints at something made ready or reworked, so the letters are rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of strategists

explanation.surface: A general's lead planner in ancient Carthage gets ready to launch an invasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to enter a party uninvited, intruding on it like an unwanted incomer.

clue.text: Scavenger in middle of Sahara repressing thirst

indicators.note: repressing means holding something down within, so the middle letters enclose the thirst word
the middle of a six-letter word is its central two letters

parts.note: the two central letters of Sahara
a yen is a craving or thirst

explanation.surface: A scavenging animal in the heart of the desert holds back its thirst.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas are carnivores known for feeding on carcasses left by other predators.

clue.text: Sucker repeatedly hit target

parts.note: to lam is to thrash, beating someone over and over
prey is the target of a hunter

explanation.surface: A gullible person keeps getting struck and is picked out as a victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a dupe, but it is the fish that clamps onto its host with a sucking mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamprey is an eel-like fish that attaches to other fish with a circular sucking mouth.

clue.text: Allotment raised to meet specifications

parts.note: a measure is an allotted portion, as in a measure of whisky
up means raised

explanation.surface: A garden plot is lifted to satisfy the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allotment' suggests a British rented garden plot, but here it is a portion handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To measure up is to reach the required standard, to be good enough.

clue.text: Clear out drain

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to leave in a hurry, to scarper
second meaning: to let liquid run out of something

explanation.definitionFit: To run off is both to flee quickly and to make water flow away from a container.

clue.text: Irregular stay, with nude dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move around, so stay and nude are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd sojourn spent dancing naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsteady means wobbly or not regular, like an uneven heartbeat.

clue.text: Gunners support non-firing weapon

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are gunners
a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge

explanation.surface: Artillerymen back up a weapon that cannot shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender thrusting sword, a blade rather than a gun.

clue.text: Discharged agent gets help

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
aid is help

explanation.surface: A fired agent receives some assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharged' suggests dismissed, but here it is a debt discharged, that is paid off.
explanation.definitionFit: A discharged debt is one that has been settled, paid back in full.

clue.text: Trouper's safe, heading off aboard wagon

indicators.note: aboard means riding inside, so the trimmed word sits within the wagon word

parts.note: a van is a wagon or covered vehicle

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: An actor on tour is secure once the leader leaves and they climb onto the wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is old British criminal slang for a safe, hence 'peterman' for a safecracker.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouper is a reliable, long-serving performer or worker, an old hand who has seen it all.

clue.text: Initially viewing mountain peak in time to see flower

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

parts.note: first letter of viewing

indicators.note: in means the peak sits inside the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time
Ben is a Scottish word for a mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: First looking at a summit, a walker arrives in time to spot a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a garden plant with clusters of small bright blossoms.

clue.text: Enforced change of leadership after troops get back

indicators.note: after means the coup letters come after the troops letters

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps
a coup is the forcible overthrow of a government

explanation.surface: After a military takeover, the soldiers come home.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to recover or regain something lost, such as money.

clue.text: Term for online currency, such as pony?

parts.note: e- is the prefix for electronic or online things
quid is slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to call a digital cash token; pony is also slang for twenty-five pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A pony is British slang for 25 pounds, which pulls toward money; here it is the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An equid is any member of the horse family, of which a pony is one example.

clue.text: Standard mass for cardinal

parts.note: par is a standard or norm
a mass of something is an amount of it

explanation.surface: A churchman celebrates a regular Mass for a cardinal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman but is used as an adjective, as in cardinal sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means of chief importance, which is what paramount means.

clue.text: Open University finally given added distinction

indicators.note: finally means the last letter

parts.note: last letter of given
a bar is an extra award added to a medal ribbon

explanation.surface: An Open University student finally earns an extra honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open University' reads as the distance-learning institution, but 'Open' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbar a door is to remove its bolt, so to unlock or open it.

clue.text: Take on extra risk with service, chasing succession of balls

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the service letters follow the cricket term

parts.note: in cricket an over is a run of six balls bowled by one bowler
a rite is a religious service

explanation.surface: A tennis player gambles more on a serve after a run of balls.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is a set of six deliveries from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: In insurance, to overwrite is to underwrite more cover than is prudent, taking on excess liability.

clue.text: Nameless dead artist's intensely dark shade

indicators.note: nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: numb limbs feel dead
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A deceased painter with no name is remembered for very dark tones.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbra is the darkest central part of a shadow, as during an eclipse.

clue.text: Dad and I voiced early cartoon character

parts.note: pop is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: voiced means spoken, so we enter the word that sounds like the letter I

parts.note: the letter I is said aloud as eye

explanation.surface: A father and child provide the voices for an old cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye the Sailor Man is a spinach-eating animated hero dating from the 1930s.

clue.text: Canny guards somewhat short of rupees, like dad

indicators.note: guards means surrounds protectively, so the canny word wraps around the trimmed word

parts.note: fly is slang for shrewd or canny

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the R is removed

parts.note: rather means somewhat

explanation.surface: A shrewd parent protects some savings, not quite enough rupees, as dads do.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatherly describes behaviour typical of a father: protective, kind, paternal.
